messages:
liam: RFC draft — eviction handoff & kernel handover (target: v1.7). need scope decision today.
liam: TL;DR: when we switch kernels (eg quantized <-> fp16), we must either atomically hand off KV/prefix state or deterministically replay to avoid duplicated/garbled tokens. proposing acceptance criteria below.
liam: Proposed acceptance criteria:
- AC1: no token duplication or omission across handoffs in our stress harness (N=1000 sessions).
- AC2: warm p95 end-to-end latency delta <= 20ms after handoff.
- AC3: replay/restore of KV context succeeds within 3s for long sessions (>1k tokens).
- AC4: automatic fallback to previous kernel on corruption detection within 200ms, with observable metric.
- AC5: rollout plan includes canary with 1% traffic, synthetic golden prompts and a blind user prompt set.
liam: owners: @natalie (canary plan), @alex (test harness + metrics), @carrie (runtime/ops).
liam: question: do customer asks (esp large-context chat) force us to add compatibility layers for multiple KV formats?

natalie: adding :eyes: on canary. i can own rollout gating and smoke checks.
natalie: need to know expected failure modes we should detect server-side vs client-side.

alex: i'll wire up the harness. basic sim command:
```
# simulate handoff at token 500
python tests/handoff_sim.py --model redwood-v1 --steps 1000 --switch-at 500 --seed 42
```
alex: harness will report dup/loss counts + latency histogram. will add a KV-serialization-diff check.

carrie: runtime notes: two practical handoff strategies we discussed earlier:
1) in-memory atomic transfer: same KV binary layout between kernels -> cheap, low-latency.
2) replay: re-run prefix tokens on new kernel when binary incompatible -> higher CPU but simpler correctness.
carrie: tradeoffs: atomic transfer needs format compatibility and careful versioning. replay needs rate limiting for tail spikes.

sam: customer angle: big customers (chat + agents) have very long sessions. if we replay, we risk tail latency spikes that violate SLAs. can we do partial handoff (only recent N keys) then background replay?

maria: heads-up, format mismatch is real: quantized kernels use compacted key layout (HFF v2) vs fp16 (HFF v1). we can convert but need deterministic test vectors.
maria: edge-case: partial key conversion may lose precision -> might change logits slightly -> downstream safety/eval differences. we should include a quality regression test set.

liam: good points. proposal: implement both paths but gate atomic transfer to kernel pairs that share KV ABI. fallback to replay with throttled background replay + streaming handoff for large sessions. update ACs to include quality regression threshold (e.g., top-1 token unchanged for > 95% of golden prompts).

natalie: canary checklist draft:
- Canary job deploy to pool B with 1% traffic.
- Run harness N=500 golden prompts every 10m.
- Alert if dup/loss > 0 or top-1 divergence > 5% or p95 latency delta > 20ms.
- Auto rollback if any hard fail.

alex: metrics to add to console: handoff_count, handoff_failures, handoff_latency_ms_p50/p95, kv_conversion_errors, top1_divergence_rate.

carrie: runtime impl notes: need feature flagging per kernel pair, and a migration tool to bump KV ABI versions. also need a fallback route table to send traffic to older pool on detection.

maria: tests: include deterministic seeds, token-by-token comparison, and a small fast-check for stochasticity. also test memory spikes during conversion.

sam: from PM: customers asking for zero-loss during business-critical flows. we should document tradeoff: atomic-only gives lower latency but restricts kernel churn. replay allows more flexibility. decision impacts product roadmap for dedicated/customers.

liam: decision call: scope for v1.7 = implement both codepaths, ship gate for atomic transfer only when ABI match, add background replay + throttling, and the canary gating from natalie's checklist. quality regression test must be part of acceptance.

natalie: ack, i'll own canary playbook and rollout runbook.

alex: i'll land test harness PR and add dashboard cards.

carrie: i'll add runtime flags, route table changes, and migration tool stub.

maria: i'll produce KV conversion validator and golden vectors.

deploy-bot: CI: tests/handoff_sim.py — 1 failed (flaky test detected). see CI run: https://ci.redwood/3456/hand-off/78

liam: noted, alex can you triage CI failure before we cut the canary?
alex: on it. quick guess: race in conversion path.

sam: please capture this decision in the PRD and RFC header: implement both handoff strategies, gate atomic transfer by ABI compatibility, add quality/regression thresholds and canary gating. I'll update product asks and customer impact notes. :thumbsup:
